thread:
Maya: Quick follow-up from the autoscale split RFC — proposal: operator-side shim handles graceful drain + local fallback heuristics, central autoscaler keeps provisioning authority. Reason: lower latency for tail requests during drain and fewer control-loop churn spikes. Thoughts? :thinking:
Arjun: Agree with goal. main worry is duplication of admission logic and policy drift between shim and autoscaler.
Maya: Plan is the shim gets a versioned policy blob (read-only), compact decision table only. Canonical policy stays in control plane; we push blobs. shim emits telemetry if it sees a mismatch.
Jun: OK. migration story? if we change schema how do we avoid sudden behavior changes?
Lia: Add a policy_epoch + checksum. shim refuses unknown major versions and falls back to safe mode (reject). Also: emit shim.policy_epoch and shim.policy_checksum metrics.
Tom: Drain semantics question — when operator initiates drain to free up GPU, do we let shim accept short requests? what's graceful timeout and behavior?
Maya: Operator exposes: drain_mode (graceful|force) and drain_deadline (secs). Shim computes remaining_deadline and accepts only if remaining_deadline > min_tail_latency. config flag `--min-tail-latency=200ms`. If too short, shim tries reroute then 429.
Priya: Try to avoid 429s — prefer provisional routing to a compatible lower-quality model variant if available (fallback to quantized or shorter context).
Maya: Agreed. Fallback ordering: local reroute -> lower-quality variant -> reject. Need a cheap compatibility check though.
Arjun: Keep compatibility metadata tiny (compat_hash per model + small capability bitmask). push with policy blob. shim uses bloom-like check: if passes, allow reroute, else skip.
ops-bot: DeployBot: policy-blob v3 pushed to cluster 'canary' by Maya at 2025-03-15T14:12Z :rocket:
Lia: Telemetry contract: add spans/tags for fallback decisions so we can correlate tail latency -> fallback. counters: shim.fallback_count{tenant, pool, reason}, gauge shim.policy_epoch, histogram shim.decision_latency_ms.
Maya: Draft proto and tiny sample config below — feedback please:
```json
{
  "policy_epoch": "2025-03-15T14:12Z",
  "min_tail_latency_ms": 200,
  "fallback_order": ["local_reroute", "lower_quality_variant", "reject"],
  "compat_hash": "sha256:abcd1234",
  "max_fallback_streak": 3
}
```
Jun: add `max_fallback_streak` — good call to prevent oscillation where shim continuously reroutes a tenant. Also consider `cooldown_ms` after a fallback.
Maya: will add `cooldown_ms` (default 30000).
Arjun: one more operational concern — who owns the canary? if shim fallback rates spike we need automated rollback or scale-up. autoscaler should subscribe to shim.fallback_count and trigger immediate scale-up if threshold exceeded.
Priya: Agree, threshold logic: fallback_rate > 5% for 1m -> autoscaler emergency bump. Also correlate model-quality regressions.
Maya: I'll open an RFC follow-up PR with schema, shim API surface, autoscaler subscription rules, and a short rollout plan (canary -> region -> global). Will include example traces and dashboards.
Tom: Sounds good. small nit: ensure the shim binary verifies blob signature (kms) — don't trust unauth config pushes.
Maya: yep, will sign blobs. thanks all :thumbsup:
